sub: Named after at-taḥrīm, “forbidding”, from lima tuḥarrimu in ayah 1
theme: Only Allah makes things lawful or unlawful. An incident in the Prophet’s ﷺ household becomes a lesson for all: protect your family, repent sincerely, and know that each person is saved by their own faith, not their relatives’.
story: Revealed in Madinah, around 7–8 AH. The Prophet ﷺ used to drink honey at the home of his wife Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. Feeling jealous, ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah agreed to tell him he smelled of maghāfīr, a gum with an unpleasant smell.

He disliked any bad smell, so he swore off honey and asked that it be kept private, not wanting to hurt Zaynab. The wife he told passed it on. Another report says the matter was Māriyah, mother of his son Ibrāhīm.

Allah revealed that only He makes things lawful, gave a way out of oaths, and called the two wives to repent. The Prophet ﷺ stayed apart from his wives for a month; people thought he had divorced them, but he had not.

sections.title: The Prophet ﷺ forbade something lawful; a secret leaked, two wives warned
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ is asked why he forbade himself something lawful to please his wives; Allah forgives and has set a way out of oaths. A secret he confided was passed on, and Allah told him. Two wives are called to repent, and warned: Allah could give him better wives.
points: Why forbid what Allah made lawful, seeking your wives’ approval?
Allah has set a way to release oaths
A confided secret passed on; Allah informed him
You two, repent; Allah, Jibrīl, the righteous and angels back him
If he divorced you, Allah could give him better wives
sections.matters: Only Allah decides what is lawful, not even the Prophet ﷺ on his own. The Quran openly records this gentle correction: even the best people are human, and what Allah left uncorrected in the Prophet’s ﷺ life is fully reliable.
sections.story: Reportedly he had drunk honey at Zaynab’s home, and ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah said he smelled of maghāfīr, so he swore off it. Another report names Māriyah. ʿUmar said the two in ayah 4 were ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah; his own warning to the wives matched ayah 5.
explained: The Prophet ﷺ had sworn off honey (in another report, Māriyah) to please his wives. Allah asks why forbid what He made lawful, and assures him of forgiveness. He has set expiation as the way out of oaths. He had told one wife in confidence; she told another. Allah informed him, and he generously mentioned only part of it.

The two wives are called to repent, since their hearts had leaned from what was right. If they kept backing each other against him, Allah is his protector, and Jibrīl, the righteous believers and the angels help him. If he divorced them, Allah could give him better wives. He never did, and they hurried to please him.
teaches: Only Allah makes things lawful or unlawful.
Don’t forbid yourself what Allah has made lawful.
Keep what is told to you in confidence.
When you correct someone, don’t expose every detail.
Even the best people slip, and repentance is the way back.
sections.hook: Ayah 3 uses the root of “news” four times: nabbaʾat, nabbaʾahā, anbaʾaka, nabbaʾaniya. Ayah 4 speaks to two (in tatūbā); ayah 5 speaks to all (in ṭallaqakunna).

sections.title: Guard your family from the Fire; sincere repentance brings gardens and light
sections.meaning: Believers must protect themselves and their families from a Fire fuelled by people and stones, kept by stern angels. Disbelievers will hear: no excuses today. Believers are called to sincere repentance, promised gardens and light on the Day. The Prophet ﷺ is told to strive firmly against disbelievers and hypocrites.
points: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire of people and stones
Stern, strong angels who never disobey Allah
Disbelievers: no excuses today, only your deeds repaid
Tawbah naṣūḥ: sins erased, gardens, and light on the Day
Strive against disbelievers and hypocrites, and be firm
sections.matters: The lesson moves from the Prophet’s ﷺ home to every believer’s home. You answer not only for yourself but for teaching your family. And for every slip, the way back is sincere repentance, before the Day when excuses are useless.
sections.story: No specific incident. Reportedly, when ayah 6 came, ʿUmar asked how they could protect their families. The Prophet ﷺ said: forbid them what Allah forbade you, and command them what Allah commanded you.
explained: Protect yourselves by obeying Allah, and your families by teaching them and guiding them to obey Him. The Fire burns people and stones (either idols or sulfur stones). Its keepers are harsh, powerful angels who carry out every command at once. On that Day disbelievers are told: make no excuses; you are only repaid for what you did.

Believers are called to tawbah naṣūḥ: regret, stop, and never return. Allah will erase sins and admit them to gardens on the Day He does not disgrace the Prophet ﷺ or the believers, their light running ahead as they pray: “Our Lord, perfect our light.” Then the Prophet ﷺ is told to strive firmly against disbelievers and hypocrites.
teaches: Teaching your family what Allah commands is your duty.
Excuses help no one on that Day; act now.
Real repentance: regret, stop, and never go back.
Ask Allah to perfect your light and forgive you.
sections.hook: Each ayah is a new call: yā ayyuha alladhīna āmanū (6), alladhīna kafarū (7), alladhīna āmanū (8), an-nabiyy (9), echoing ayah 1. Page 561 begins at ayah 8.

sections.title: Nūḥ and Lūṭ’s wives lost; Pharaoh’s wife and Maryam are believers’ models
sections.meaning: Two examples for the disbelievers: the wives of Nūḥ and Lūṭ, married to righteous prophets, yet their marriages could not save them from the Fire. Two for the believers: Pharaoh’s wife, who asked for a house near Allah in Paradise, and Maryam, who guarded her chastity, believed and obeyed.
points: Wives of Nūḥ and Lūṭ: married to prophets, still in the Fire
Pharaoh’s wife: “My Lord, build me a house near You in Paradise”
“Save me from Pharaoh, his deeds and the wrongdoing people”
Maryam: chaste, believed her Lord’s words and books, devout
sections.matters: It completes the surah’s lesson. Marriage to a prophet saved no one without faith, and marriage to a tyrant harmed no one with faith. Each person stands on their own faith and deeds: a reminder for the Prophet’s ﷺ wives, and for everyone.
sections.story: No specific incident. Pharaoh’s wife was Āsiyah bint Muzāḥim. Reportedly she believed in Mūsā, was tortured by Pharaoh, made this duʿāʾ, and was shown her house in Paradise before she died.
explained: The wives of Nūḥ and Lūṭ lived with two righteous prophets, yet betrayed them in faith. It was never a betrayal of chastity: they refused to believe. Reportedly one called Nūḥ mad, and the other told her people about Lūṭ’s guests. Their husbands could not help them, and they were told: enter the Fire.

Pharaoh’s wife lived with the worst tyrant, yet believed. She asked Allah for a house near Him in Paradise and rescue from Pharaoh, and his disbelief could not harm her. Maryam guarded her chastity; Allah had Jibrīl breathe into her garment, and she conceived ʿĪsā. She believed her Lord’s words and books and was devoutly obedient.
teaches: No relationship can replace your own faith.
A hard environment can’t stop a sincere believer.
Ask Allah for Paradise and rescue from wrongdoers.
Chastity, faith and obedience raised Maryam’s rank.
sections.hook: Ayat 10 and 11 both open ḍaraba Allāhu mathalan: first for alladhīna kafarū, then for alladhīna āmanū. The surah ends on al-qānitīn, echoing qānitāt in ayah 5.

groups.text: Why forbid yourself what Allah made lawful to please your wives? Allah forgives, and has set a way to release oaths.
The Prophet ﷺ confided in one wife; she told another. Allah informed him, and he mentioned only part of it.
You two, repent. If you team up against him, Allah, Jibrīl, the righteous believers and the angels support him.
If he divorced you, his Lord could give him better wives: devout, believing, obedient, repentant and worshipful.
Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire of people and stones. Disbelievers will be told: no excuses today.
Repent sincerely: Allah will erase sins and grant gardens, with light on the Day He does not disgrace the believers.
Strive against the disbelievers and hypocrites, and be firm with them; Hell is their home.
Nūḥ’s and Lūṭ’s wives betrayed their prophet husbands in faith, and their marriages could not save them from the Fire.
Pharaoh’s wife asked for a house near Allah in Paradise. Maryam guarded her chastity, believed, and was devoutly obedient.

1.explain: Lima tuḥarrimu: why forbid? A caring question, not harsh blame. The Prophet ﷺ had sworn off something lawful to please his wives. Wa Allāhu ghafūrun raḥīm: Allah has forgiven him, and no blame remains.
1.why: Reportedly he drank honey at Zaynab bint Jaḥsh’s home, and ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah agreed to say he smelled of maghāfīr. He swore not to drink it again. Another report says it was about Māriyah, mother of his son Ibrāhīm; the honey report is more authentic.

2.explain: Taḥillat aymānikum: Allah has set expiation as the way to release an oath when breaking it is better. This became a rule for all believers. Mawlākum: He looks after you, All-Knowing and Wise.

3.explain: Asarra: he confided something to one wife, and she passed it on. Allah told him through revelation not recorded in the Quran. ʿArrafa baʿḍahu: he generously mentioned only part of it. “Who told you?” “Al-ʿAlīm al-Khabīr.”
3.why: Reportedly the secret was his oath about honey, which he asked her to keep private (another report: about Māriyah). Reportedly Ḥafṣah was the one he confided in, and she told ʿĀʾishah.

4.explain: Tatūbā and qulūbukumā address two wives. Ṣaghat: their hearts had leaned from what was right. If they back each other against him, Allah is his mawlā, with Jibrīl, the righteous believers (reportedly including Abū Bakr and ʿUmar) and the angels.
4.why: ʿUmar was asked who the two wives were and said: ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah. He also told the Prophet ﷺ, during the month apart, that Allah, His angels, Jibrīl and the believers were with him, and this ayah echoed his words.

5.explain: A warning: if he divorced them, Allah could give him better wives: submitting, believing, qānitāt (obedient), repentant, worshipping, sāʾiḥāt (fasting, or emigrating), previously married or not. He never divorced them; they hurried to please him.
5.why: ʿUmar reportedly told the wives: “Stop troubling the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or Allah may give him better wives than you.” This ayah came in almost those words.

6.explain: Qū anfusakum wa ahlīkum: protect yourselves by obeying Allah, and your families by teaching them His commands. Its fuel is people and stones (either idols or sulfur). Its keepers are stern, strong angels who obey without delay.

7.explain: Said to disbelievers on the Day: don’t make excuses. The time for excuses is over. You are only repaid for what you did.

8.explain: Tawbah naṣūḥ: sincere repentance: regret the sin, leave it, and never return. ʿAsā here is a promise. On that Day the believers’ light runs ahead, and as the hypocrites’ light goes out, they pray: “Perfect our light.”

9.explain: Jāhid: strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, with proof and, where needed, in battle. Ughluẓ: be firm with them, not soft. Their final home is Hell, a wretched destination.

10.explain: Ḍaraba Allāhu mathalan: Allah gives an example. Nūḥ’s and Lūṭ’s wives betrayed them in faith, never in chastity. Reportedly one called Nūḥ mad; the other told her people about Lūṭ’s guests. A prophet husband could not save them.

11.explain: Pharaoh’s wife, Āsiyah, believed in Mūsā and was reportedly tortured for it. She asked for a house ʿindaka, near Allah, in Paradise, and rescue from Pharaoh, his deeds and his people. His disbelief could not harm her.

12.explain: Maryam, daughter of ʿImrān, guarded her chastity. Jibrīl breathed into her garment by Allah’s command, and she conceived ʿĪsā. She believed her Lord’s words and books, and was of al-qānitīn, the devoutly obedient.
